backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 (keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64, so grad accumulation halves). In a fixed 300 s budget on an A100, more optimizer steps usually beats larger batches for a small model.
backlog.title: Lower total batch to 2**18

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 (accumulation steps = 2 if seq len 2048, otherwise adjust). Optionally scale MATRIX_LR by about 0.9 if unstable.
backlog.title: Lower total batch to 2**17

backlog.spec: Change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the LR decays linearly over more of the time budget.
backlog.title: Warmdown ratio 0.7

backlog.spec: Change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.3, giving more time at full LR.
backlog.title: Warmdown ratio 0.3

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.05 so the LR does not fully reach zero at the end of the warmdown.
backlog.title: Final LR fraction 0.05

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.03 to add a brief LR warmup. This may help stability at higher LRs.
backlog.title: Short warmup

backlog.spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.05.
backlog.title: Matrix LR 0.05

backlog.spec: Raise EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.8.
backlog.title: Embedding LR 0.8

backlog.spec: Double UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008.
backlog.title: Unembedding LR 0.008

backlog.spec: Halve SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.25 to stabilize the per-layer scalars.
backlog.title: Scalar LR 0.25

backlog.spec: Lower Muon WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1.
backlog.title: Weight decay 0.1

backlog.spec: Raise WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.3.
backlog.title: Weight decay 0.3 for short run

backlog.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS to (0.8, 0.99) for smoother second-moment estimates on the embeddings.
backlog.title: Adam beta2 0.99

backlog.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS to (0.9, 0.95).
backlog.title: Adam beta1 0.9

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 6 (model_dim = 384 with ASPECT_RATIO 64). A smaller model gets more steps in 300 s. Then try ASPECT_RATIO 96 if the code permits, to keep the width up.
backlog.title: Depth 6 wider-per-time

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 10, keeping ASPECT_RATIO at 64, and lower DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32 if it OOMs. Check whether the larger model pays off despite fewer steps.
backlog.title: Depth 10

backlog.spec: Set ASPECT_RATIO = 80 with DEPTH = 8 (dim 640, rounded to a multiple of HEAD_DIM if the code requires it). The wider model may use the A100 better.
backlog.title: Aspect ratio 80

backlog.spec: Set HEAD_DIM = 64 to get more attention heads. This is cheap to test.
backlog.title: Head dim 64

backlog.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN to "SSSSL" or "SSL". The change shifts the balance of full-context to half-context layers, and shorter windows are faster.
backlog.title: Window pattern SSSS+L last

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN = "SSSS". The code should still force the final layer to full attention. This tests the speed gain from cheaper attention.
backlog.title: All-short windows except last

backlog.spec: If the logit softcap is 15, change it to 30. Otherwise add a softcap of 20 using tanh on the logits before the loss.
backlog.title: Softcap logits lower

backlog.spec: Reduce the MLP hidden expansion from 4x to 3x. That frees compute for more steps. Alternatively keep 4x and test it against this.
backlog.title: Squared-ReLU to SwiGLU-free tweak: MLP ratio 3

backlog.spec: If torch.compile is used on the model, try mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs'. Compile time is not counted, and faster kernels give more steps in 300 s.
backlog.title: Disable torch compile mode tweaks: max-autotune

backlog.spec: Set DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 32. This lowers memory and may be faster on the A100 through better cache behavior. Check that accumulation adjusts automatically.
backlog.title: Device batch 32 with accumulation

backlog.spec: Change the Muon momentum schedule so it ramps to 0.97 within 100 steps rather than the current ramp. If the schedule is already like this, raise the final momentum from 0.95 to 0.97.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup shorter/higher

backlog.spec: Reduce the Newton-Schulz iterations in Muon from 5 to 4 to save time per step, if the code exposes this value.
backlog.title: Muon NS steps 4

backlog.spec: Make sure the output projections of attention and MLP are zero-initialized. If they already are, change the residual-lambda init from 1.0 to 0.9 for the x0 skip scalars.
backlog.title: Zero init of projection and value-embedding gate tweaks

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown with a cosine shape: with progress p in the warmdown phase, use lr_mult = FINAL_LR_FRAC + (1-FINAL_LR_FRAC)*0.5*(1+cos(pi*p)).
backlog.title: Cosine-shaped warmdown

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**17 (about 131K tokens per optimizer step) so the 300 s budget gives roughly 4x more optimizer steps. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE at 64 so that grad accumulation shrinks accordingly. If the code asserts that TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE is divisible by DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE*MAX_SEQ_LEN, make sure it still holds. Leave all LRs unchanged.
backlog.title: Total batch 2**17 with depth 6

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH=4 and ASPECT_RATIO=128 so model_dim is 512 (a multiple of HEAD_DIM 128, giving 4 heads). The shallower model has cheaper, faster steps and sees more tokens within 300 s. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Depth 4 with wider dim (ASPECT_RATIO 128)

backlog.spec: Disable the value-embedding (ResFormer-style) path in alternating layers: don't create the value-embedding tables and skip the gated addition to v in attention. This removes large embedding parameters and their Adam updates and should speed up steps. Make the code simpler by deleting the path entirely, and make sure the optimizer param groups no longer reference it.
backlog.title: Remove value embeddings

backlog.spec: Halve MAX_SEQ_LEN only if it is defined in train.py and not imported from prepare.py. If it is imported, instead change the window pattern to all-short windows, 'SSSS', so that attention is cheaper at every layer, with the final layer forced to be full as the code already does. The aim is higher throughput per second.
backlog.title: Sequence length 1024 with larger device batch

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO=0.05 and WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.4 and keep FINAL_LR_FRAC=0.05. Combine the small positive signals into one run. Check that the schedule function handles warmup as a fraction of the elapsed time progress.
backlog.title: Time-based LR warmup 5% plus warmdown 0.4

backlog.spec: Keep an exponential moving average of model weights (decay 0.999 per step, updated every step with torch._foreach_lerp_ on a copy of the parameters in bf16/fp32). Swap the EMA weights in just before the final evaluation call, without touching the evaluation code itself, by copying the EMA into the model params after the training loop ends. Only do this if it does not touch the eval call or the summary printing.
backlog.title: Weight EMA for evaluation

backlog.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.0 for Muon. With only about 300 s of training the model is far from overfitting, so decay just slows learning. Also try keeping the decay schedule untouched if it is tied to the LR multiplier.
backlog.title: Lower weight decay to 0 on short run

backlog.spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06 and reduce the Muon Newton-Schulz iteration count from 5 to 4 to save per-step time. This is a single bolder optimizer change targeting a faster per-step rate in the small model.
backlog.title: Muon LR 0.06 plus Newton-Schulz 4 steps

backlog.spec: Reduce the logit softcap constant from 15 to 30, if it is currently 15, or otherwise set it to 30, and raise UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008. Both changes together make the output head learn faster in the short budget.
backlog.title: Logit softcap 30 and untied-lm_head LR 0.008

backlog.spec: Use a smaller effective batch early in training: for the first 30% of the time budget use grad accumulation giving 2**17 tokens per step, then switch to 2**19 for the rest. Implement it by making the number of accumulation micro-steps a function of the progress fraction, and scale the loss by the current accumulation count. Leave the LR schedule as it is.
backlog.title: Batch-size ramp

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17 (grad accumulation steps become 1 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 at seq len 2048 if applicable; otherwise reduce DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE accordingly). Multiply MATRIX_LR by 0.7 and keep other LRs. This is a bold step-count increase.
backlog.title: Total batch 2**17 with scaled LRs

backlog.spec: Remove the value-embedding (ResFormer-style per-layer value embedding) branches and their parameters and gates from the model, so attention uses only the plain projected v. This frees parameters and embedding-optimizer work per step, and tests whether they pay for themselves in 300 s. Keep the code simpler as a result.
backlog.title: Remove value embeddings

backlog.spec: Change the logit softcap constant (currently probably 15 or 30 in the forward pass, where logits = softcap * tanh(logits/softcap)) to 10 if it's 15+, or leave the form unchanged and just reduce the constant. Tests the stabilizing effect on a short run.
backlog.title: Lower logit softcap to 15

backlog.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.05. In a 300 s run with few steps, strong decay of 0.2 may hurt fitting; test a much weaker value.
backlog.title: Weight decay 0.05 on Muon

backlog.spec: Set EMBEDDING_LR = 0.3 and UNEMBEDDING_LR = 0.008 together. This rebalances the Adam groups: slower token-embedding updates, faster lm_head updates.
backlog.title: Embedding LR 0.3 and unembedding LR 0.008

backlog.spec: Set MATRIX_LR = 0.05 and WARMUP_RATIO = 0.03 together. The warmup stabilizes the larger LR; both earlier small gains pointed toward a slightly higher LR on the depth-6 model.
backlog.title: Short warmup plus Muon LR 0.05

backlog.spec: Initialize every block's attention c_proj and MLP c_proj weights to zero (if not already) and scale the init std of the token embedding to 0.5 of the current value. This makes the network start as identity and can speed early learning in a 300 s run.
backlog.title: Untied-init scaling: zero-init attention and MLP output projections

memo: Helped: shrinking the model. Slot 3 (DEPTH 8->6) scored 1.0828/1.0833 over 2 runs, delta -0.0314, and is the incumbent at mean_adjusted 1.0831. It carries a tripwire flag, so check that first. Did not help: a bigger model (DEPTH 10, +0.0815), and most schedule edits (cosine warmdown +0.0589, warmdown 0.7 +0.0033, warmdown 0.3 +0.0005, warmup/warmdown mix +0.0006). Also no help: EMA (+0.8027), HEAD_DIM 64 (+0.0063), MLP 3x (+0.0024), DEPTH 4 with ASPECT_RATIO 128 (+0.0020), shorter Muon ramp (+0.0023), SSSS windows (-0.0002, a tie). Small gains that were rejected: Muon LR 0.06 with fewer Newton-Schulz steps (-0.0021) and FINAL_LR_FRAC 0.05 (-0.0042, measured on the depth-8 base). Slot 6 max-autotune scored 1.0811 but was invalid for going over budget. Next: audit the tripwire. Then re-test FINAL_LR_FRAC 0.05 and the slot 10 Muon change on the depth-6 base, alone and combined. Then try DEPTH 5 and batch-size or sequence-length changes for throughput.
